ai.literal: Distress to us to remain behind, he who went to a far distance thinking of, fragrant flowers felt ashamed, the eyes.
ai.translation: Thinking of him who went far away, leaving me with nothing but distress, my eyes have wept so much that they now shrink in shame before fragrant flowers.
ai.modern: நமக்குத் துன்பத்தை விட்டுவிட்டுத் தொலைதூரத்திற்குச் சென்ற காதலரை நினைத்து வருந்துவதால், என் கண்கள் அழகு கெட்டு நறுமணமுள்ள மலர்களுக்கு அஞ்சி நாணமடைகின்றன.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the physical toll of separation on the heroine's eyes. Her lover has departed to a distant land ('சேண் சென்றார்'), leaving her behind in deep distress ('சிறுமை நமக்கு ஒழிய'). By constantly thinking of him and weeping ('உள்ளி'), her eyes have lost their natural luster, becoming red and swollen. Previously, her beautiful eyes were compared to fresh, fragrant flowers ('நறுமலர்') and outshone them; now, having lost their beauty, the eyes feel ashamed ('நாணின') to even look at those flowers.

ai.literal: The beloved one's lack of love, they speak, it seems, having turned pale and shedding tears, the eyes.
ai.translation: My eyes, turning pale and shedding tears, seem to proclaim the lack of love of my beloved.
ai.modern: என்னை விரும்பிய காதலரின் அன்பில்லாத தன்மையை, பசலை நிறமடைந்து கண்ணீர் வடிக்கும் என் கண்கள் பிறருக்குச் சொல்வது போலத் தோன்றுகின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments her physical deterioration due to separation. Her eyes have turned pale and are constantly shedding tears. She poetically imagines that her weeping eyes are not merely expressing her grief, but are actively announcing to the world that her beloved has failed to show grace and love by staying away. The word 'pōlum' emphasizes this comparison, showing how her silent suffering is made public by her eyes.

ai.literal: The fact of separation, very much, they make known, it seems, the shoulders that swelled on the day of union.
ai.translation: My shoulders, which swelled with joy on the day of our union, now seem to clearly announce his departure by wasting away.
ai.modern: கூடிய நாளில் பருத்திருந்த என் தோள்கள், இப்போது மெலிந்துபோய் அவர் பிரிந்து சென்றதை எல்லோருக்கும் மிக நன்றாக அறிவிப்பது போல் தோன்றுகின்றன.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments the physical toll of separation from her lover. Her shoulders, which once swelled with beauty and joy on the day they united, have now shrunk and wasted away. This dramatic physical change acts as a public announcement of his departure, making her private grief visible to everyone. The word 'வீங்கிய' describes the fullness of her shoulders during union, while 'அறிவிப்ப' highlights how their current thinness betrays her secret sorrow.

ai.literal: Losing their bamboo-like fullness, the fresh bracelets slip off; having lost their companion, the shoulders have withered, losing their original beauty.
ai.translation: As my companion has departed, my shoulders have lost their original beauty and withered; and losing their bamboo-like fullness, my bright bracelets slip off.
ai.modern: துணைவனாகிய காதலர் பிரிந்து சென்றதால், என் தோள்கள் தம்முடைய பழைய அழகை இழந்து வாடிவிட்டன; மூங்கில் போன்ற பருத்த தன்மையை இழந்து மெலிந்ததால், என் கைகளில் உள்ள பசுமையான வளையல்களும் கழன்று விழுகின்றன.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the heroine laments her physical decline caused by the separation from her lover. She describes her shoulders, which were once as shapely and smooth as bamboo ('பணை'), now shrinking so much that her bright bracelets ('பைந்தொடி') slip off ('சோரும்'). This physical wasting is directly linked to the departure of her companion ('துணை நீங்கி'), which has caused her shoulders to lose their natural, original beauty ('தொல்கவின்') and wither ('வாடிய தோள்').

ai.literal: Along with bracelets shoulders to grow thin I suffer; him cruel that calling feeling pained.
ai.translation: I suffer as my shoulders waste away and my bracelets slip off; yet, it pains me even more to call him cruel.
ai.modern: வளையல்களுடன் தோள்களும் மெலிந்து போவதால் நான் வருந்துகிறேன்; ஆனால், அதற்காக அவரை இரக்கமற்றவர் என்று சொல்வதற்கும் என் மனம் நொந்து தயங்குகிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses her deep conflict during separation. Her grief has caused her to lose so much weight that her shoulders have shrunk, causing her bracelets to slip off. While she suffers from this physical decline, she finds it even more painful to blame her lover and call him cruel for leaving her. Her love is so profound that she would rather bear the physical wasting of her body than speak ill of her beloved.

ai.literal: Will you obtain dignity, O heart, by telling the cruel one about the distress of my wasting shoulders?
ai.translation: O my heart! Will you gain any dignity by going and telling that cruel man about the distress of my wasting shoulders?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! என் வாடுகின்ற தோள்களின் துன்பத்தைப் பற்றி அந்த இரக்கமற்றவரிடம் போய்ச் சொல்வதால் நீ ஏதேனும் பெருமையைப் பெறுவாயோ?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks to her own heart, which is eager to seek out her departed lover. She calls him 'the cruel one' (கொடியார்) because he left her to pine in separation. Her shoulders have grown thin and wasted (வாடுதோள்) from grief, causing a visible distress or clamor (பூசல்). She asks her heart if there is any dignity or self-respect (பாடு) to be gained by exposing her pathetic state to someone who was unfeeling enough to leave her.

ai.translation: The moment we relaxed our tight embrace, even slightly, paleness spread over the forehead of my simple beloved who wears beautiful bracelets.
ai.modern: தழுவியிருந்த கைகளைச் சற்றே தளர்த்திய உடனே, அழகிய வளையல்களை அணிந்த இப்பேதை பெண்ணின் நெற்றி பசலை நிறமடைந்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet depicts the extreme sensitivity of the heroine to even a momentary separation. The hero observes that when they slightly loosened their embrace, her forehead immediately turned pale with grief. The word 'paim-toṭi' refers to her beautiful bracelets, and 'pēthai' highlights her innocent, tender nature. Her instant physical reaction of turning pale shows how deeply she feels even the slightest distance from her lover.

ai.translation: Just because a cool breeze passed through the space between us during our embrace, the large, rain-like eyes of this simple girl have turned sallow.

ai.explanation: This couplet describes the extreme sensitivity of the heroine's love and her inability to bear even the briefest separation. The hero remarks that during their tight embrace, a tiny gap occurred, allowing a cool breeze to pass between their bodies. This momentary and minute distance was felt so intensely by the naive heroine that her large, moist, rain-like eyes immediately lost their natural luster and turned sallow. The word 'pasappu' refers to the yellowing or paleness of the skin and eyes caused by the grief of separation, highlighting the depth of her attachment.

ai.literal: The pallor of the eyes has indeed attained distress, having seen what the bright-foreheaded lady did.
ai.translation: Seeing the self-afflicting grief of this bright-foreheaded lady, even the pallor of her eyes seems to have fallen into deep distress.
ai.modern: ஒளிபொருந்திய நெற்றியை உடையவள் தனக்குத்தானே செய்து கொண்ட துன்பத்தைக் கண்டு, அவளுடைய கண்களில் படர்ந்த பசலை நிறமும் கூடத் துன்பத்தை அடைந்துவிட்டது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the extreme state of the heroine's grief during separation from her lover. Her eyes have developed 'pasappu', a pale, sallow discoloration that signifies deep yearning. The poet beautifully personifies this pallor, suggesting that even the pallor itself has become distressed upon witnessing how much the bright-foreheaded lady ('ஒண்ணுதல்') is suffering. Instead of merely being a symptom of her pain, the pallor is depicted as a sympathetic observer that is overwhelmed by her sorrow.
